clue.text: Beetle has one motor at speed

definitions.note: read as 'what a beetle has', a noun phrase

parts.note: a motor is a car
one is the article a
speed is pace; 'at' just places it alongside

explanation.surface: An insect-shaped car, the VW Beetle, apparently boasts an engine running fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The motor is read first although the clue lists 'one' before it. 'Beetle' invites the VW car, but the definition is what a beetle carries on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard protective shell on an animal's back, the kind of armour a beetle wears.

clue.text: Catch Queen following sentimental stuff

indicators.note: following means the royal piece comes after the other piece rather than before it

parts.note: corn is mawkish, sentimental material
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen caught out after some soppy, sentimental fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: To corner someone is to trap or catch them where they cannot escape.

clue.text: Banker, say, busier pocketing single note

indicators.note: pocketing means putting something away inside, so one word holds the others within it

parts.note: busier, of a design, means more elaborate or fancier
I is the Roman numeral one
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A banker, already busier, slips a lone banknote into a pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: I and N go in together just after the F of FANCIER, giving F-IN-ANCIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A financier manages large sums of money, and a banker is one example, hence the 'say'.

clue.text: Puritan accepting heartless evil is beginning

indicators.note: heartless means the middle of the word is cut out, leaving only its outer letters
accepting means taking something in, so the prim person's word receives the other inside

parts.note: a puritan is a prude, someone easily shocked
evil with its two middle letters removed

explanation.surface: A strait-laced person tolerating a little wickedness marks the start of a downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelude is an introductory piece or event, the opening that precedes the main matter.

clue.text: Somewhat tight, in fact firm, initially

definitions.text: Somewhat tight, in fact firm, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: the first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: Describing something, perhaps a lid, that starts a bit tight and turns out firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: something a bit tight and in fact firm at first is stiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff means rigid or hard to move, which is exactly a firm, tight state.

clue.text: In eating, our man devours pig

indicators.note: In tells the solver the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: runs from the end of eating through to the start of devours

explanation.surface: A man at the table who wolfs down his food like a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'devours' a verb of eating, but it only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmand is a glutton, and calling someone a pig means they eat greedily.

clue.text: Local putting green round tee

indicators.note: round means placed around, so the green word goes about the golf item

parts.note: green means inexperienced or naive
a tee is named from the letter T

explanation.surface: A local golfer on the putting green walks round to the tee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting green' is a golf phrase in the surface; 'green' alone is the inexperienced word, and 'putting' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A native is someone born in a place, which is what calling a person a local means.

clue.text: Card game is nowhere near over

parts.note: nowhere near means far away
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A card game that is a long way from finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Faro is an old gambling game played with cards against a banker.

clue.text: Senseless trial with on air broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pointless courtroom trial televised live to the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the two parts of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Irrational means lacking reason or logic, which is what senseless describes.

clue.text: Precipitation almost cold during autumn?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word for chilly loses its final letter
during gives the word for 'inside', which is spelt out here as letters of the answer

parts.note: raw weather is cold and damp
during means in, as in 'in the night'
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: Asking whether the chilly wet weather is typical of autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that fall here is the American name for the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainfall is water falling from the sky, the commonest form of precipitation.

clue.text: Some prefer video to get passionate

indicators.note: Some means only a portion of the words that follow is taken

parts.note: spans the end of prefer and the start of video

explanation.surface: Some people would rather watch a video to get worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervid means intensely enthusiastic, burning with feeling, so it matches passionate.

clue.text: Obstacle about to block pub outing

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: to block means to sit in the way, lodged inside something else

parts.note: a ride is an outing, a trip out
CA is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Something placed to stop a group's trip to the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A barricade is a barrier put up to stop movement, a kind of obstacle.

clue.text: Group of women hurt embracing sweetheart

indicators.note: embracing means holding in the arms, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to hurt is to harm
the heart, or middle letter, of sweet

explanation.surface: Wounded women's group hugging a darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' is a crossword staple: not a lover but the central letter of sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women of a household in some traditional Muslim societies, so a group of women.

clue.text: Nag perhaps, and chores are undone

indicators.note: undone means taken apart, so these letters are loosened and remade

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone nags about household jobs left unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a verb about scolding over chores, but it is the noun for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is a horse, often a poor one, and a racehorse is one kind, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Shrinking in action being seduced

indicators.note: in places one piece within another, the bashful word set inside the deed word

parts.note: a deed is an action
coy means bashful, shrinking from attention

explanation.surface: Someone shy who finds themselves won over once things get going.
explanation.definitionFit: To decoy someone is to lure them into a trap, so being decoyed is being enticed or seduced.

clue.text: Stood our ground in the open

indicators.note: ground means crushed up, as in a mill, so the letters are broken and remixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: We refused to back down, standing firm out in plain view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stood our ground' is a stock phrase, which hides that ground is the mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoors means outside buildings, in the open air.

clue.text: Dressing declared forbidden before date

indicators.note: before means the first piece is placed ahead of the date piece
declared means spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: forbidden means banned, which is said like a music group
a date can mean a period or era, an age

explanation.surface: An outfit officially prohibited ahead of a romantic evening out.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandage is a strip of material wrapped over a wound, which is what a medical dressing is.

clue.text: My lord purchases old cape

indicators.note: purchases means buys and takes in, so the deity word holds the next piece

parts.note: the Lord is God
O is the standard abbreviation for old
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: An aristocrat buys an antique cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My lord' reads as a form of address; 'My' alone is the exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: 'My!' and 'Goodness!' are both mild exclamations of surprise, interchangeable interjections.

clue.text: Adult hammered and confused

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult
hammered means struck hard, bashed

explanation.surface: A grown-up who got drunk and ended up muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammered' suggests drunk in the surface, but it means beaten here.
explanation.definitionFit: Abashed means embarrassed and disconcerted, thrown into confusion.

clue.text: Hospital department admitting stroke is severe

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, as a hospital admits a patient, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: A&E, accident and emergency, is the British casualty department
a stroke of a blade or bat is a cut

explanation.surface: Casualty takes in a patient whose stroke is serious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' plays on the medical sense; here it is a slicing blow. A&E is the UK term for an emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: Acute describes something intense or serious, especially an illness, matching severe.

clue.text: Gossip about the French holiday home

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the chatter word goes round the French article

parts.note: gossip is chat
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Idle talk about a French family's place in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden cabin, often rented as a ski or holiday lodge.

clue.text: Old boy with hearing thing

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a court hearing is a session

explanation.surface: An old man with a hearing aid or some such gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thing' means a fixation, as in 'having a thing about' something.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a thing is a preoccupation, so having a thing for something is having a fixation on it.

clue.text: Bench is put in order

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a long wooden seat with a high back
second meaning: to sort out or arrange

explanation.surface: A seat being arranged neatly in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word names a high-backed wooden bench; as a verb it means to resolve or arrange.

clue.text: Opposed to criminal's first caper

parts.note: anti means against

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the lawbreaker word

parts.note: the opening letter of criminal

explanation.surface: Someone against a crook's leading role in a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caper' suggests a heist, but it means a playful prank.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a silly or grotesque action, a caper or piece of foolery.

clue.text: Car shortly carrying a learner driver

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so one word bears the others inside

parts.note: shortly means soon
taken as written
a learner driver displays an L plate

explanation.surface: A vehicle soon to have a novice motorist on board.
explanation.walkthrough: A saloon is the British name for a sedan car.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is a car with a closed body and separate boot, so a type of car.

clue.text: Blasting birds finally making owl noises

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word for birds

parts.note: the closing letter of birds
owls hoot

explanation.surface: Firing at game birds at last, while owls call in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting and blasting both mean firing a gun at something.

clue.text: He's nastier, unhinged, showing strength?

indicators.note: unhinged means deranged, knocked off its hinges, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man who grows meaner and more deranged, maybe a sign of power.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that heartiness is only loosely strength, more vigour than muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartiness is robust vigour and good health, a kind of physical strength.

clue.text: Young woman left halfwit

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A girl abandoned by a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lass is a girl or young woman, chiefly in Scottish and northern English usage.
